title: Actors — who may act
body: A party that authors changes: a human or an AI agent. An HQDM `party`. Authentication is a token the deployment verifies to one of these actors; the actor is never a string the client declares. Recorded by decision dec-auth.

title: Actor kind
body: human / agent / service. The system is a collaboration between humans and AI, so who (or what) an actor is matters — but it does not by itself grant authority; a grant does.

title: Actor status
body: active / revoked. A revoked actor keeps its history (append-only) but its grants no longer authorize.

title: Grants — model-driven authorization
body: A grant is an HQDM `association` between an actor and a scope. The DO reads these rows to decide who may write — so authorization is model-first (data you can query and render), not code buried in the server. Reads stay open; every mutation needs a grant.

title: Granted actor
body: The actor this grant empowers — a ref into `actors`, the participant end of the association.

title: Scope
body: read / write / admin. write authors rows; admin also changes the schema (a design-level act). The DO's write-gate checks these; a bootstrap-admin anchor in the deployment breaks the genesis chicken-and-egg before any grant exists.

title: Actor → Grants
body: Each grant names the actor it empowers; following this edge gives an actor's authority.
